광화문 해치.x: Haechi (haetae) is a mythical creature said to tell right from wrong and drive away evil forces. The pair of haechi guarding Gwanghwamun is said to have been placed to stop the fire energy of Gwanaksan, which faces the gate head-on, from reaching the palace. They are the first gateway of the wish, built into the rebuilt Gyeongbokgung, that it would never burn again.

근정전 드므.x: On the stone terrace of Geunjeongjeon sit wide vessels called deume. Legend says that when the fire demon came to set the palace ablaze, it saw its own hideous face reflected in the water of the deume and fled in fright. They also really served as fire-water tanks for putting out fires.

경회루의 용.x: Legend says two bronze dragons were sunk beneath Gyeonghoeru in Gyeongbokgung to protect the palace from fire. In 1997 a bronze dragon was actually found while the pond was being dredged, confirming the legend. It is a relic of the Joseon people's wish to subdue the fire energy of Gwanaksan with water and dragons.

아미산 굴뚝.x: Amisan is a small flower garden behind Gyotaejeon, the queen's quarters, said to have been built with soil dug from the Gyeonghoeru pond. Its four hexagonal chimneys carried smoke from Gyotaejeon's ondol floors through underground flues, and the auspicious patterns carved on their walls make them beautiful ornaments in their own right. They are designated a Treasure.

향원정과 물불.x: Hyangwonjeong is a two-story hexagonal pavilion on an island in the middle of a pond; its name means 'fragrance spreading far'. In 1887 Korea's first electric light was lit at Geoncheonggung, north of the pond. Because the generator was driven with water drawn from the pond, people called the light 'water fire'. It flickered off and on so often that it was also nicknamed the 'loafer's light'.

무학대사와 왕십리.x: When Master Muhak, searching for a site for the capital, reached today's Wangsimni, an old man ploughing a field scolded his ox: "You're as foolish as Muhak!" The old man told him to "go ten li further northwest" and vanished, and that spot became the site of Gyeongbokgung. The place name Wangsimni is said to come from 'go ten li further'.

인왕산 선바위.x: When the walls of Hanyang were being built, Master Muhak wanted the huge Seonbawi rock on Inwangsan inside the walls, while Jeong Do-jeon wanted it outside. Jeong argued that "inside, Buddhism will flourish; outside, Confucianism will", so it was left outside, and Muhak is said to have sighed, "In five hundred years you will remember my words." Many people still pray at Seonbawi, believing it has spiritual power.

치마바위.x: King Jungjong, who came to the throne through a coup, was forced by the coup leaders to send away his beloved Queen Sin. Whenever the deposed queen missed the king, she spread her pink skirt over a rock on Inwangsan, and Jungjong eased his heart by gazing at it from Gyeongbokgung. The rock is called Chimabawi, the Skirt Rock, and the tale lives on as a legend of tender love.

숭례문 현판.x: The name board of Sungnyemun, the Great South Gate, is said to have been written by Grand Prince Yangnyeong, King Sejong's elder brother. Unlike other gates its characters are written vertically; a feng shui story holds that the characters meaning 'exalting propriety' were stood upright to block, like a counter-fire, the fierce fire energy of Gwanaksan rushing toward the palace.

청계천 광통교와 신덕왕후.x: When Queen Sindeok, King Taejo's most beloved second queen, died, a grand tomb called Jeongneung was built inside the capital. But King Taejong, who hated his stepmother, moved the tomb outside the walls and used its stones to rebuild Gwangtonggyo Bridge so that the people would walk over them. Even today you can see the tomb stones laid upside down under the bridge.

세검정.x: Changuimun (Jahamun), between Inwangsan and Bugak, is the pass through which the rebel army entered and seized the palace in the Injo Restoration. The nearby Segeomjeong (洗劍亭) is said to take its name from the plotters washing their swords (洗劍) there to seal their resolve.

남산 국사당.x: On Namsan (Mongmyeoksan) stood Guksadang, a shrine where people prayed for the nation's peace. When the Japanese colonial government built the Chosen Shrine, they moved Guksadang beside Seonbawi on Inwangsan, where shamanic rites and ceremonies continue to this day.

아차산과 온달.x: General Ondal, husband of Goguryeo's Princess Pyeonggang and known as 'Ondal the Fool', set out to win back land lost to Silla and is said to have been killed by an arrow in a battle near Achasanseong. A touching legend adds that his coffin would not move until the princess caressed it.

백제 위례성.x: Wiryeseong was Baekje's first capital, built on the Han River by Onjo, who came down from Goguryeo; Pungnaptoseong and Mongchontoseong in Songpa are thought to be its remains. Inside its huge rammed-earth walls the capital culture of five centuries of Baekje flourished, showing that Seoul has been an important capital since the Three Kingdoms period.

백제 개로왕과 한강.t: King Gaero of Baekje and the Han River
백제 개로왕과 한강.x: When Hanseong Baekje fell to an invasion by King Jangsu of Goguryeo, King Gaero of Baekje is said to have been captured near Achasan and met his end. This history shows the fierce struggle of the Three Kingdoms over the Han River and the tragic end of Hanseong Baekje.

석촌동 고분.x: At Seokchon-dong remain Goguryeo-style stone-piled tombs built like steps. They are evidence that the Baekje royal family came down from Goguryeo and are believed to be tombs of kings from Hanseong Baekje's golden age.

광나루.x: Gwangnaru was a major ferry across the Han River and a strategic crossing fought over by Baekje, Goguryeo and Silla. Facing Achasan across the river, it holds the history of a waterway where the rise and fall of the Three Kingdoms crossed paths.

김알지와 석탈해.x: When a white rooster crowed at night, people gathered in Gyerim forest. A golden chest hung from a branch, and the child who came out of it was Kim Al-ji. As founder of the Gyeongju Kim clan, he became the root of Silla's royal house. Around the same time, Seok Tal-hae crossed the sea in a chest, won a house site through his wits, and rose to the throne. A golden chest and a wooden chest: two children who opened thousand-year Silla. Imagine that beginning beneath the trees of Gyerim.

선덕여왕의 지혜.x: When a painting of peonies arrived from Tang without any butterflies, Queen Seondeok knew the flowers had no scent. When frogs croaked at Okmunji pond, she knew enemy soldiers were hiding nearby and defeated them. These, together with foretelling the day of her death and where she would be buried, are her 'three prophecies'. The wisdom of the queen who read the sky beneath Cheomseongdae protected Silla. Follow her star-reading mind before the 27-layer stone tower.

미추왕 죽엽군.x: When enemies closed in on Gyeongju, soldiers with bamboo leaves tucked behind their ears suddenly appeared, drove them off and vanished. When people went to the royal tomb, bamboo leaves lay piled before King Michu's tomb. Because the spirit of the late king had become soldiers to defend the kingdom, that army is called the Bamboo-Leaf Army. The bamboo of Daereungwon is its trace. Walk around the tomb and remember the bamboo-leaf soldiers.

에밀레종.x: When the Sacred Bell of King Seongdeok was being cast, the metal would not set and kept cracking. Legend says the bell was completed only after a child was put into the molten metal, and that its sound rings 'emille', like a child calling its mother. It is a folk legend not found in official histories, but that is how people remembered the bell's long echo. See the flying-angel reliefs and hear the bell at the museum. That lingering sound is the legend's name.

무영탑(아사달과 아사녀).x: While the Baekje stonemason Asadal was building Seokgatap at Bulguksa, his wife Asanyeo watched the pond every day, believing they would meet when the pagoda's shadow appeared on the water. When no shadow ever appeared, she threw herself into the pond. Because it has no shadow, Seokgatap is called the Shadowless Pagoda. The couple's waiting remains before the pagoda standing beside Dabotap. Look at the pond and search for the shadow.

만파식적과 문무왕.x: King Munmu vowed to become a dragon and protect the kingdom even after death, and was buried at Daewangam in the East Sea. His son King Sinmun built Gameunsa and made a flute from bamboo found in the sea. Because blowing it made enemies retreat and the waves fall calm, it was called Manpasikjeok. Pass the stone pagodas of Gameunsa Site and look out at Daewangam to see the sea of the king who became a dragon. Imagine, in the sound of the waves, the swells the flute once stilled.

처용.x: When Cheoyong, son of the Dragon King of the East Sea, lived in Gyeongju, the spirit of plague violated his wife. Instead of raging, Cheoyong sang and danced, and the spirit, moved, swore never to enter any place bearing Cheoyong's face. After that, people hung Cheoyong's face on their gates to ward off disease. It is a Silla story of driving off disaster with song and dance. Remember why Cheoyong's face became a talisman.

김유신과 천관녀.x: Kim Yu-sin swore to his mother that he would never again visit the house of Cheongwannyeo. One day, drunk and dozing on horseback, his horse carried him to that familiar house. On waking, Kim Yu-sin cut off the horse's head for breaking his vow, and with that resolve he became the great general who unified the Three Kingdoms. Cheongwansa temple was later built where Cheongwan lived. It is the story of a single vow that led Silla to unification.

이차돈의 순교.x: When the king wished to make Buddhism the faith of the nation but his officials objected, Ichadon offered his own neck. When the sword fell, white blood spurted and flowers rained from the sky. Seeing this miracle, people accepted Buddhism, and Silla went on to become a Buddha land. The white blood and the rain of flowers recall the door to a thousand years of Buddhism opened by martyrdom. It is the place where one man's faith changed a nation.

지귀(심화요탑).x: Jigwi, who adored Queen Seondeok, fell asleep while waiting before the palace. The queen did not wake him; she simply left her bracelet and went on. When Jigwi awoke and saw the bracelet, his longing blazed up like fire and he turned into a fire spirit. The pagoda built to quench that fire is Simhwayotap: the story of love turned to flame. Imagine the spark left by Queen Seondeok's bracelet.

문전본풀이.t: Myth of the Door God (Munjeon Bonpuri)

울산바위.x: When rocks from all over the country were summoned to form Geumgangsan, the rock that set out from Ulsan was so huge that it arrived late. Seeing that all the peaks were already taken, the disappointed rock sat down in Seoraksan, and people came to call it Ulsanbawi, the Ulsan Rock.

흔들바위.x: Above Gyejoam hermitage on Seoraksan is a rock that sways when pushed by hand yet never falls. One story says a monk placed it there to test his mind; another says only those with a sincere heart can move it.

오세암.x: A five-year-old child lived at a hermitage on Seoraksan with his uncle, a monk. While the monk went down to fetch food, heavy snow cut off the path. When he returned the next spring, the child was gone and only a small Buddha remained. Because the child is said to have attained Buddhahood under the care of the Bodhisattva of Compassion, the hermitage is called Oseam, 'the hermitage of the five-year-old'.

낙산사 홍련암.x: When Silla's Great Master Uisang was praying in a seaside cave at Naksan, a red lotus rose above the waves and the Bodhisattva of Compassion appeared on it. Uisang built a hermitage on the spot where he met the bodhisattva and named it Hongnyeonam, Red Lotus Hermitage. Together with the founding story of Naksansa, it remains a hermitage on a rock pounded by the waves.

대관령 국사성황.x: A maiden of Haksan in Gangneung scooped up and drank the sun reflected in a spring and bore a child. That child grew up to be Beomil, a great monk of late Silla, and after his death people believed he became the guardian god of Daegwallyeong. The Gangneung Danoje Festival begins by bringing this guardian god down from Daegwallyeong.

진도 신비의 바닷길.t: The Miracle Sea Road of Jindo

혹부리 영감.t: The Old Man with a Lump

정조와 사도세자.t: King Jeongjo and Crown Prince Sado
정조와 사도세자.x: Crown Prince Sado, son of King Yeongjo, died locked in a rice chest amid factional strife. His son Jeongjo, who witnessed his father's death as a child, moved his father's tomb to Suwon after becoming king and built the planned city of Hwaseong beside it, honoring his father all his life.

화성 축성과 거중기.t: Building Hwaseong and the Lifting Crane
화성 축성과 거중기.x: King Jeongjo entrusted the design of the fortress to the Silhak scholar Jeong Yak-yong, who built a 'geojunggi', a crane using pulleys, to lift heavy stones with ease. Thanks to it, Hwaseong was completed faster and sturdier than planned, and the whole process was recorded in detail in 'Hwaseong Seongyeok Uigwe', helping make it a UNESCO World Heritage site.

방화수류정과 용연.x: Banghwasuryujeong, whose name means 'seeking flowers and following willows', is Hwaseong's most beautiful pavilion, and its view together with the Yongyeon pond below is superb. A military lookout that is also an outstanding pavilion, it is counted among the finest examples of Joseon architecture, combining function and beauty.

용주사와 효심.x: King Jeongjo founded Yongjusa near Yungneung to pray for the soul of his father, Crown Prince Sado. The temple keeps a bell filled with Jeongjo's devotion and a Buddhist altar painting said to be by Kim Hong-do, and is called 'the temple of filial piety'.

혜경궁 홍씨.x: Lady Hyegyeong, wife of Crown Prince Sado and mother of King Jeongjo, recorded her husband's tragedy and palace life in her memoir 'Hanjungnok'. For her 60th birthday, Jeongjo held a grand banquet at Hwaseong Haenggung to honor her.

궁예의 최후.x: Gungye, of Silla royal blood, founded Later Goguryeo (Taebong), called himself the Maitreya Buddha and grew ever more tyrannical. In the end his subordinate Wang Geon took his throne, and because Gungye fled and wept aloud on Myeongseongsan, the mountain is called the 'Mountain of Tears'.

신라 경순왕.x: When King Gyeongsun, Silla's last ruler, could no longer defend the kingdom, he handed it over to Wang Geon of Goryeo to spare his people. After he died in Gaegyeong, there was a plan to bury him in Gyeongju, but objections that 'a king's bier may not travel more than 100 li' led to his burial in Yeoncheon, making his the only Silla royal tomb outside Gyeongju.

숭의전과 고려.x: Joseon built Sungeuijeon by the Imjingang River to honor Goryeo's founder Wang Geon and later Goryeo kings and meritorious subjects. It is a rare shrine where one dynasty kept up the rites of the dynasty before it, a place to remember Goryeo's history.

왕건과 궁예.x: Wang Geon, who won fame serving Gungye, was raised to the throne by officials who had turned against Gungye's tyranny, and founded Goryeo. He ousted the lord he had served to open a new dynasty, and the crossed fates of the two men became the prelude to the unification of the Later Three Kingdoms.

용문사 은행나무.x: The ginkgo of Yongmunsa in Yangpyeong is about 1,100 years old and the largest in East Asia. One story says Crown Prince Maui planted it on his way to Geumgangsan after Silla fell; another says Great Master Uisang's walking stick took root. It is also said to cry out when great events befall the nation.

나옹선사와 신륵사.x: Silleuksa, beside the Namhangang River, is where the late-Goryeo master monk Naong passed away. Its name is said to come from taming a fierce dragon-horse with a divine bridle (神勒), and because of the brick pagoda on a riverside rock it is also called the 'Brick Temple'.

세종대왕.x: Sejong, the fourth king of Joseon, was a sage king who created Hangeul and brought science, music and agriculture to flower. He rests with Queen Soheon at Yeongneung in Yeoju, a site so auspicious that people said 'Yeongneung added a hundred years to Joseon's life'.

마의태자.x: Son of Silla's King Gyeongsun, he opposed handing the kingdom to Goryeo, went alone into Geumgangsan and ended his life wearing hemp clothes (麻衣), hence the name 'Crown Prince Maui'. Legend says the tree he planted along the way is the ginkgo of Yongmunsa.

행주대첩과 행주치마.t: The Battle of Haengju and the Haengju Apron
행주대첩과 행주치마.x: In 1593, during the Imjin War, General Gwon Yul and some 3,000 troops crushed 30,000 Japanese soldiers at Haengjusanseong. The Battle of Haengju is counted among the three great victories of the war, and it is said the word 'Haengju chima' (apron) came from the women of the fortress carrying stones in their skirts to help the soldiers.

권율 장군.x: Gwon Yul was a great general of the Imjin War who defeated the Japanese at the Battle of Ichi and at Haengju, later becoming supreme commander of the entire Joseon army. His son-in-law was Yi Hang-bok, famous from the tale of 'Oseong and Hanum'.

처인성과 김윤후.x: During the second Mongol invasion in 1232, at a small earthen fort in Cheoin-bugok (today's Yongin), the monk Kim Yun-hu and local villagers stood their ground, shot dead the Mongol commander Salietai with an arrow and drove off the enemy. It is a shining moment of Goryeo's defense, when people of low status protected the nation.

포은 정몽주.x: Jeong Mong-ju, a loyal subject of late Goryeo, tried to protect the declining dynasty to the end and was killed on Seonjukgyo Bridge by Yi Bang-won's faction. He is famous for answering Yi Bang-won's poem 'Hayeoga' with his 'Dansimga': 'Though I die and die again, a hundred times over…'. His tomb is in Yongin.

단군과 참성단.x: Chamseongdan on the summit of Manisan is an altar where Dangun is said to have offered rites to heaven. The flame for the National Sports Festival is still lit here, and it is revered as a sacred place symbolizing the origin of the Korean people.

강화 고인돌.x: The table-type dolmen of Bugeun-ri, Ganghwa, is a huge Bronze Age tomb whose capstone alone weighs dozens of tons; together with Gochang and Hwasun it is a UNESCO World Heritage site. It is a symbol of the megalithic culture raised on this land thousands of years ago.

고려의 강화 천도.x: When the Mongols invaded in the 13th century, Goryeo moved its capital from Gaegyeong to Ganghwa and resisted for about 39 years. The Tripitaka Koreana was carved during this period, when the narrow strait (Yeomha) served as a shield.

전등사 나부상.x: At the four corners of the eaves of Jeondeungsa's main hall are 'nabusang', naked women holding up the roof. Legend says the master carpenter carved the tavern keeper who betrayed him and ran away, so she would hold up the eaves forever while listening to the Buddha's teachings.

삼랑성(정족산성).x: Samnangseong, which embraces Jeondeungsa, is a mountain fortress said to have been built by Dangun's three sons. It is also a site of national defense, where Yang Heon-su's troops defeated the French during the 1866 French expedition and safeguarded the Annals of the Joseon Dynasty.

온달과 평강공주.x: 'Ondal the Fool' married Goguryeo's Princess Pyeonggang and became a fine general. He died fighting near Ondalsanseong on the Namhangang while trying to win back land taken by Silla, and a touching legend says his coffin would not move until the princess caressed it.

도담삼봉과 정도전.x: Dodamsambong, three peaks rising from the Namhangang, is the symbol of Danyang. It is said that Jeong Do-jeon, architect of Joseon, played here as a child and took 'Sambong' (three peaks) as his pen name.

사인암.x: Sainam, one of the Eight Scenic Views of Danyang, is named after Yeokdong U Tak, a Goryeo official holding the post of 'Sain', who loved to visit it. Its sheer cliff and pine trees look like a painting.

중앙탑.x: The seven-story stone pagoda of Tappyeong-ri, Chungju, is called the 'Central Pagoda' because Unified Silla is said to have built it to mark the center of the land. It is the tallest surviving stone pagoda of Unified Silla.

충주 고구려비.x: The Chungju Goguryeo Stele is the only Goguryeo stele in South Korea, showing that 5th-century Goguryeo extended its power to the Namhangang basin. Along with the Gwanggaeto Stele, it is a precious monument conveying the spirit of Goguryeo.

논개와 의암.x: When Jinjuseong fell in the Imjin War, the gisaeng Nongae embraced a Japanese general on a rock below Chokseongnu and threw herself into the Namgang River. The rock is called Uiam (義巖), the 'Righteous Rock', in honor of Nongae's loyalty.

진주대첩과 김시민.t: The Siege of Jinju and Kim Si-min
진주대첩과 김시민.x: In 1592, Jinju magistrate Kim Si-min and 3,800 soldiers held off an attack by 20,000 Japanese troops, winning a great victory. Together with Haengju and Hansando, the Battle of Jinju is counted among the three great victories of the Imjin War.

이순신과 한산대첩.t: Yi Sun-sin and the Battle of Hansando
이순신과 한산대첩.x: In 1592, Yi Sun-sin routed the Japanese navy off Hansando using the hagikjin, a 'crane wing' formation. This victory secured control of the South Sea and turned the tide of the war.

삼도수군통제영.t: The Naval Command of the Three Provinces
삼도수군통제영.x: Sebyeonggwan in Tongyeong was the main building of the Tongjeyeong, the headquarters commanding the navies of Gyeongsang, Jeolla and Chungcheong. The very name 'Tongyeong' comes from this Tongjeyeong.

통영 미륵산.x: From the top of Mireuksan, the islands and sea of Hallyeosudo spread out before you. It is Tongyeong's finest view over the waters Yi Sun-sin defended, and a cable car makes it easy to reach.

하회마을과 류성룡.x: Hahoe is a traditional village where the Pungsan Ryu clan has lived for generations, and the hometown of Seoae Ryu Seong-ryong, who led the nation as chief state councillor during the Imjin War and wrote 'Jingbirok'. Named 'Hahoe' (river turning) because the Nakdonggang wraps around it, it is a World Heritage site.

하회탈과 허도령.t: The Hahoe Masks and Young Heo
하회탈과 허도령.x: A touching legend says that young Heo, guided by a divine revelation, was carving masks behind a sacred straw rope when a maiden who loved him peeked in; he died before finishing the chin of the last mask, Imae. That is why the Imae mask has no chin.

퇴계 이황과 도산서원.x: Toegye Yi Hwang, the great scholar who systematized Joseon Neo-Confucianism, declined office and returned home to teach students. Dosanseowon, built in his honor, is a center of Confucian learning and appears on the 1,000-won bill.

봉정사.x: Geungnakjeon Hall of Bongjeongsa in Andong is Korea's oldest wooden building. Its founding tale says a disciple of Great Master Uisang folded a phoenix from paper and let it fly; where it landed, the temple was built.

월영교와 원이 엄마.x: Woryeonggyo Bridge in Andong comes from the love story of 'Woni's mother', who, mourning her husband who died before her, wove sandals from her own hair and placed a heartfelt letter in his coffin. The bridge is beautiful on moonlit nights.

땅끝과 갈두.x: Ttangkkeut (Land's End) in Haenam is the southernmost point of the Korean peninsula's mainland. Its old name was Galdu, and the sunrise and sunset over the archipelago seen from here are spectacular. The Ttangkkeut Tower and observatory mark the end of the land.

미황사 창건설화.x: Mihwangsa on Dalmasan has a founding tale: a stone boat arrived carrying scriptures and a Buddha statue, and a cow carrying them lay down for the last time on the spot where the temple was built. The name is said to join 'mi' (beautiful) with 'hwang', the sound of the cow's lowing.

고산 윤선도와 녹우당.x: Noguudang is the old house of the family of Gosan Yun Seon-do, the Joseon poet who wrote 'Eobusasisa'. It is called 'Nogu' (green rain) because when the nutmeg forest sways in the wind it looks like green rain falling. The self-portrait of Gongjae Yun Du-seo has also been handed down in this family.

다산 정약용의 유배.x: Dasan Jeong Yak-yong was exiled to Gangjin in the Sinyu persecution and spent 18 years there. Staying at Dasan Chodang, he wrote some 500 volumes including 'Mongmin Simseo', turning his place of exile into the cradle of Joseon Silhak.

백련사 동백.x: Baengnyeonsa in Gangjin is linked to Dasan Chodang by a forest path, along which the exiled Jeong Yak-yong and the abbot Hyejang came and went, sharing learning and tea. The camellia forest around the temple turns red in winter.

이성계와 전주.x: Jeonju is the ancestral home of Yi Seong-gye, King Taejo who founded Joseon. His royal portrait is enshrined at Gyeonggijeon, and Omokdae is where he held a feast after returning from defeating Japanese pirates at the Battle of Hwangsan.

견훤의 후백제.x: In late Silla, the general Gyeon Hwon from Sangju founded Later Baekje with Jeonju as its capital and for a time vied for supremacy among the Later Three Kingdoms. But after his sons fought over the throne, he met the sad fate of submitting himself to Wang Geon of Goryeo.

서동과 선화공주.x: A tale says that Seodong of Baekje (later King Mu), in love with Silla's Princess Seonhwa, had children sing a song saying 'Princess Seonhwa meets Seodong every night' (Seodongyo), spreading the rumor until he married her.

익산 미륵사지.x: Mireuksa in Iksan, founded by King Mu, was Baekje's largest temple, and Korea's oldest and largest stone pagoda (the Mireuksa Stone Pagoda) still stands there. A record that the queen founded the temple was found in the sarira enshrinement inscription.

백제 무왕.x: King Mu of Baekje, believed to be the hero of the Seodong tale, sought to revive Baekje, placing a royal palace in Iksan (Wanggung-ri) and founding Mireuksa. He is said to have planned to make Iksan a second capital.

이순신과 전라좌수영.t: Yi Sun-sin and the Jeolla Left Naval Base
이순신과 전라좌수영.x: Yeosu was home to the headquarters of the Jeolla Left Naval Command led by Yi Sun-sin during the Imjin War. Here he built turtle ships and trained sailors to defend the South Sea, and its central building is Jinnamgwan.

거북선.x: The turtle ship, the assault vessel Yi Sun-sin sent against the Japanese navy, had a back covered with iron plates and spikes so enemies could not board, and fired cannons from its dragon head. It played a major role in the battles of Hansan and Sacheon.

낙안읍성.x: Naganeupseong in Suncheon keeps its walls of earth and stone and its village of thatched houses intact, a living Joseon-era walled town where people still live today.

순천만.x: Suncheon Bay is a world-class wetland of vast reed beds and mudflats, visited by migratory birds such as hooded cranes. The S-shaped waterway and reeds at sunset are spectacular.

송광사와 지눌.x: Songgwangsa in Suncheon is the 'Temple of the Sangha Jewel', which produced sixteen National Preceptors. It is the center of practice where Goryeo's National Preceptor Bojo Jinul founded a community to renew Buddhism.

수로왕과 구지가.x: Six golden eggs descended from heaven onto Gujibong and six children were born; Suro, the first to hatch, became King Suro, founder of Geumgwan Gaya. The song people sang then is Gujiga, which begins 'Turtle, O turtle…'.

허황옥과 쌍어문.t: Heo Hwang-ok and the Twin Fish
허황옥과 쌍어문.x: Heo Hwang-ok, King Suro's queen, is said to have crossed the sea by boat from the distant 'Kingdom of Ayuta'. The twin fish motif (ssangeomun) found all over Gimhae is said to be a trace of her.

금관가야.x: Centered on Gimhae, Geumgwan Gaya produced fine iron and prospered through trade with Nangnang and Wa, leading the Gaya confederacy. The Daeseong-dong tombs yielded a flood of relics showing its power.

대성동 고분.x: The Daeseong-dong tombs belong to Geumgwan Gaya's ruling class; splendid iron armor, iron ingots and pottery found there have earned them the name 'royal tombs of Gaya'. They show that Gaya was a kingdom of iron.

팔만대장경.x: Hoping to repel the Mongol invasion through the power of the Buddha, Goryeo spent 16 years carving the Buddhist canon onto more than 80,000 woodblocks. This Tripitaka Koreana has been preserved intact for about 750 years in the Janggyeong Panjeon of Haeinsa and is a World Heritage.

해인사 창건.x: Haeinsa was built on Gayasan in the reign of Silla's King Aejang by two monks, Suneung and Ijeong, with royal support. True to its name, 'wisdom clear as the sea' (Haein), it has carried on as a site of Hwaeom practice.

최치원과 홍류동.x: Choe Chi-won, the great scholar of late Silla, turned his back on a corrupt world, went into Gayasan and lived in seclusion at Nongsanjeong in Hongnyudong Valley. One day, it is said, he vanished as an immortal, leaving only his hat and shoes.

영암사지.x: The Yeongamsa site in Hapcheon is an old temple site at the foot of Hwangmaesan; its twin-lion stone lantern and stone terraces are counted among the masterpieces of Unified Silla stone art.

아랑 전설.x: Arang, daughter of the magistrate of Miryang, resisted a clerk who tried to assault her, was unjustly killed and left below Yeongnamnu. After that each new magistrate died in strange circumstances, until a bold magistrate met Arang's ghost, heard her story and punished the culprit, setting her grievance to rest.

사명대사와 표충사.x: Great Master Samyeong of Miryang led monk soldiers against the Japanese in the Imjin War, and after the war went to Japan as a diplomat-monk and brought back some 3,000 captives. Pyochungsa is the temple that honors him.

밀양 얼음골.x: A mysterious valley where ice forms in rock crevices in midsummer and warm steam rises in winter. Designated a natural monument, this Miryang landmark is famous as a place to escape the heat.

만어사 종석.x: The stones of the scree field below Maneosa are called 'bell stones' because they ring clearly like a bell when struck. Legend says they are fish of the East Sea turned to stone.

의상과 선묘낭자.x: Seonmyo, a maiden who loved Great Master Uisang while he studied in Tang China, became a dragon to guard his sea route when he left for Silla, and when he built Buseoksa she drove off those who hindered him by floating a huge rock in the air. That rock is Buseok, the 'floating stone'.

부석사와 부석.x: Buseoksa in Yeongju, founded by Great Master Uisang, is the head temple of the Hwaeom school, and its Muryangsujeon Hall is one of Korea's most beautiful wooden buildings. Beside Muryangsujeon is the Buseok rock said to have been floated by Seonmyo.

소수서원과 주세붕.x: Sosuseowon, founded by Punggi magistrate Ju Se-bung, was Korea's first seowon to receive royal recognition (saaek). Honoring An Hyang, it opened a new path for Confucian education, and later Toegye Yi Hwang petitioned for its royal charter.

무섬마을.x: Museom Village in Yeongju is a village wrapped by a winding river, a quiet traditional village once reachable only by a single-log bridge. It is called 'Museom' because it seems like an island floating on the water.

직지와 흥덕사.x: 'Jikji Simche Yojeol', printed at Heungdeoksa in Cheongju in 1377, is the world's oldest surviving book printed with movable metal type, 78 years earlier than Germany's Gutenberg Bible. It is listed in UNESCO's Memory of the World.

상당산성.x: Sangdangsanseong in Cheongju is a mountain fortress dating back to the Three Kingdoms period; its present walls were rebuilt in stone under King Sukjong of Joseon. It was a sturdy defensive stronghold overlooking the city of Cheongju.

세조와 정이품송.t: King Sejo and the Jeongipumsong Pine
세조와 정이품송.x: A story says that when King Sejo's palanquin, on its way to Songnisan, was about to catch on a pine branch, the tree lifted its branch by itself to clear the way, so Sejo granted the pine the official rank of Jeongipum (second rank).

법주사 팔상전.x: Palsangjeon at Beopjusa in Boeun is Korea's only five-story wooden pagoda, enshrining the Palsangdo paintings that depict the Buddha's life in eight scenes. It is the symbol of Beopjusa, the great temple on the slopes of Songnisan.

백제의 미소.x: The Rock-carved Buddha Triad of Yonghyeon-ri, Seosan, is a Baekje Buddha carved into rock, called 'the Smile of Baekje' for its gentle, bright smile that changes with the direction of the light. It is a masterpiece of Baekje sculpture.

해미읍성.x: Haemieupseong in Seosan is a Joseon-era walled town with well-preserved walls and gate towers, where Yi Sun-sin once served as a military officer. It also holds the painful history of the persecution of Catholics in late Joseon.

수덕사.x: Sudeoksa on Deoksungsan in Yesan is an old temple said to have been founded in Baekje times; its main hall, built in the Goryeo period, is one of Korea's oldest wooden buildings.

추사 김정희.x: Chusa Kim Jeong-hui of Yesan was a great Joseon scholar and calligrapher who perfected his original 'Chusa style' of writing. 'Sehando', painted during his exile on Jeju, is counted a masterpiece embodying a scholar's integrity.

신사임당과 율곡.x: Ojukheon in Gangneung is the house where Shin Saimdang, a model of the wise mother, gave birth to and raised her son Yulgok Yi I. Shin Saimdang appears on the 50,000-won bill, and Yulgok and Ojukheon on the 5,000-won bill.

경포대.x: A charming saying goes that from Gyeongpodae, one of the Eight Views of Gwandong, you can see five moons: in the sky, the sea, the lake, your wine cup and your beloved's eyes. Gyeongpo Lake and the East Sea are seen at a glance.

강릉 단오제.x: The Gangneung Danoje Festival, held for over a thousand years to honor the mountain god of Daegwallyeong and the Guksa Seonghwang, is on UNESCO's list of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. Shaman rites, the Gwanno mask dance and swinging are performed.

단종의 유배.x: Danjong, who became king at twelve, had his throne taken by his uncle Grand Prince Suyang (King Sejo) and was exiled to Yeongwol at seventeen. After the six martyred ministers' attempt to restore him failed, he ended his short life here.

청령포.x: Cheongnyeongpo is a place of exile surrounded by the river on three sides with a cliff behind, an island that is not an island. Stone towers the young Danjong is said to have piled while longing for Hanyang remain, along with the pine 'Gwaneumsong' that witnessed his tears.

엄흥도와 장릉.x: After Danjong died, despite the threat that anyone recovering his body would have three generations of their family wiped out, Yeongwol's local official Eom Heung-do secretly gathered and buried it. That spot later became Jangneung, Danjong's royal tomb.

단종애사.x: The stories surrounding the tragic life and death of the boy king Danjong are called 'Danjong Aesa'. Shrines and legends honoring Danjong remain all over Yeongwol, and the Danjong Cultural Festival is still held every year.

송상현과 동래성.x: When the Imjin War broke out, Dongnae magistrate Song Sang-hyeon faced the onrushing Japanese army, declaring 'It is easy to die fighting, but hard to lend you the road', and defended the fortress to the end before dying a martyr. The Battle of Dongnaeseong symbolizes Busan as a city that defended the nation.

금정산 금샘과 범어사.x: It is said that golden fish came down from heaven to play in a rock well atop Geumjeongsan, so it was called 'Geumsaem' (golden well), and the temple built beside it 'Beomeosa' (Temple of the Heavenly Fish). It is a great temple founded by Great Master Uisang.

최치원과 해운대.x: The name 'Haeundae' is said to come from Choe Chi-won, the great scholar of late Silla, who on his way to Gayasan was so taken by this seaside scenery that he carved his pen name 'Haeun' (sea cloud) on a rock on Dongbaekseom.

태종대.x: Taejongdae, the coastal cliffs of Yeongdo in Busan, takes its name from the legend that Silla's King Taejong Muyeol rested and practiced archery here after unifying the Three Kingdoms. Strange rocks, cliffs, Sinseondae and the lighthouse form a superb view.

팔공산 동화사.x: Donghwasa on Palgongsan is a great temple founded in Silla times, named Donghwasa (Paulownia Flower Temple) because 'paulownia blossoms bloomed in the dead of winter'. A huge Unification Medicine Buddha prays for reunification, overcoming the pain of division.

갓바위 기도.x: The seated stone Buddha on the Gwanbong peak of Palgongsan is called Gatbawi because it wears a broad hat-shaped stone on its head. It is said to grant one wish to anyone who prays sincerely, so worshippers come all year round.

공산전투와 신숭겸.t: The Battle of Gongsan and Sin Sung-gyeom
공산전투와 신숭겸.x: In 927, when Wang Geon of Goryeo was badly defeated by Gyeon Hwon of Later Baekje around Palgongsan (Gongsan) and his life was in danger, General Sin Sung-gyeom put on Wang Geon's clothes and fought in his place, dying to save him. A story says Daegu's name 'Palgong' (eight lords) comes from the eight generals who died in this battle.

부인사와 선덕여왕.x: Buinsa on Palgongsan is a temple where a memorial rite for Silla's Queen Seondeok is held every year, and in Goryeo times it housed the first Tripitaka Koreana. It is a place where the Silla people's devotion to Queen Seondeok lives on.

우암 송시열.x: Uam Song Si-yeol, leader of the Noron faction and a great scholar of late Joseon, was active in Hoedeok, Daejeon. Uam Historic Park and Namganjeongsa, filled with his traces, form the heart of Daejeon's scholarly culture.

동춘당 송준길.x: Dongchundang, named after Song Jun-gil's pen name, is a detached house in Daedeok, Daejeon, and a treasure showing the dignity of Joseon gentry houses. Together with Uam Song Si-yeol, he represents the scholarly culture of Hoedeok.

계족산성.x: A Baekje mountain fortress on the ridge of Gyejoksan in Daejeon; today a red-clay trail around it has become a famous place for barefoot walking. The mountain is called 'Gyejok' (chicken's foot) because it resembles a foot.

뿌리공원과 효.x: Ppuri (Roots) Park in Daejeon is a rare theme park about Korean family names, gathering monuments to the origins of each clan. It is Daejeon's symbolic space honoring ancestors and filial piety.

반구대 암각화.x: The Bangudae Petroglyphs on a cliff of Daegokcheon in Ulsan are rock drawings of whales, tigers, deer and more carved by prehistoric people, considered the world's oldest record of whaling. They are a National Treasure and a World Heritage site.

천전리 각석.x: On the Cheonjeon-ri rock near Bangudae, prehistoric geometric patterns and writings left by Silla's hwarang are carved side by side, layering time from prehistory to Silla on a single rock.

처용과 처용암.x: Gaeunpo in Ulsan is the setting of the Cheoyong tale, in which Cheoyong, son of the Dragon King of the East Sea, drove away the spirit of disease with song and dance. The rock from which Cheoyong is said to have emerged is called 'Cheoyongam'.

대왕암과 문무왕비.x: Daewangam in Ulsan is a seaside rock where, legend says, the queen of Silla's King Munmu sank to become a dragon guarding the nation even after death. Blue sea, coastal pines and strange rocks make a superb view.

무등산 입석대.x: Ipseokdae and Seoseokdae near the summit of Mudeungsan in Gwangju are columnar joints standing like a folding screen; true to the name 'Mudeung' (beyond compare), they are a natural monument of unrivaled beauty.

김덕령 장군.x: General Kim Deok-ryeong of Gwangju raised a righteous army in the Imjin War, but despite his outstanding valor he was falsely accused and unjustly killed. Chungjangsa on the slopes of Mudeungsan honors him, and Gwangju's 'Chungjang-ro' comes from his posthumous title.

고경명과 의병.t: Go Gyeong-myeong and the Righteous Army
고경명과 의병.x: When the Imjin War broke out, the Gwangju scholar Go Gyeong-myeong raised a righteous army and died a martyr with his two sons at the Battle of Geumsan. The shrine honoring him is Pochungsa, which is why Gwangju is called 'Uihyang', the town of righteousness.

양림동 근대.x: Yangnim-dong in Gwangju is a modern history village where missionaries arrived in the early 20th century and built schools, hospitals and Western-style buildings. Old Western houses, hanok and alley art blend here, part of Gwangju as the 'town of art'.

운주산성과 백제부흥운동.t: Unjusanseong and the Baekje Restoration Movement
운주산성과 백제부흥운동.x: Unjusanseong in Sejong is said to have been a base of the Baekje restoration movement, where refugees fought to revive their kingdom after Baekje fell. From the summit you can picture Baekje's last dream.

비암사와 백제 유민.x: Biamsa in Sejong is a temple said to have been built by Baekje refugees to soothe the sorrow of their lost kingdom, where a Baekje-style Amitabha stele dated to the Gyeyu year was found. It is a temple holding Baekje's last breath.

세종대왕과 세종시.x: Sejong Special Self-Governing City is a multifunctional administrative city named after King Sejong, the sage king who created Hangeul. Spaces embodying Hangeul and Sejong's spirit are found throughout the city.

금강 이응다리.x: Ieung Bridge (Geumgang Pedestrian Bridge) across the Geumgang in Sejong is a round footbridge modeled on the Hangeul letter 'ㅇ' (ieung), one of the world's longest pedestrian-only bridges. Lit up at night, it is Sejong's new landmark.
